title: Bash in a Flash: The No-Stress Cheat Sheet
subtitle: Simple commands you can use right away to move around, inspect files, and stay out of trouble.

intro.title: Start Here
paragraphs: If the terminal feels intimidating, this guide keeps it light and practical. Learn a few commands, then repeat them until they feel natural.
Each section includes copy-ready commands and plain-English explanations so you can build confidence fast.

items.title: See where you are
items.body: Use this first whenever you are unsure of your location.

items.title: List files
items.body: Start with a simple list, then switch to detailed mode.

callout.text: Use Tab to autocomplete names and avoid typos.

blocks.title: 2) Files You Will Use Every Day

items.title: Create and remove
items.body: Make directories, create empty files, and remove carefully.

code.content:
mkdir notes
touch todo.txt
rm todo.txt

callout.text: Double-check before running rm. Deleted files are usually gone for good.

items.title: Copy and move
items.body: Duplicate files or rename and move them in one command.

code.content:
cp draft.txt draft-backup.txt
mv draft.txt notes/draft.txt

items.title: Read file content
items.body: Use quick views before opening an editor.

code.content:
cat notes/draft.txt
head -n 5 notes/draft.txt
tail -n 5 notes/draft.txt

items.title: Use quotes
items.body: Wrap paths with spaces: cd "My Folder".

items.title: Start with ls
items.body: List files before removing or moving anything.

items.title: Read command help
items.body: Try command --help whenever you are unsure.

footer.heading: You Are Officially Bash-Capable
footer.text: A handful of commands used well beats a giant cheat sheet you never practice.
